newsitem.title: GERMANY: Trade-boosting Kohl off to Argentina, Brazil, Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Trade-boosting Kohl off to Argentina, Brazil, Mexico.

text.p: Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl plans to visit Argentina, Brazil and Mexico on a seven-day trade-boosting tour starting on Saturday, a Bonn government spokesman said on Monday.

Spokesman Peter Hausmann told journalists that Kohl would be visiting the "three most important countries" in Latin America as part of the German government's 1995 "Latin American concept" promoting links with the region.
"Kohl will honour the development of democracy and market economics in the whole region," Hausmann said.
Kohl will start his trip by visiting Argentina for two days, where he is due to meet President Carlos Menem for talks and address the Senate in a speech, Hausmann said.
He will join celebrations marking the 100th anniversary of the Goethe German school in Buenos Aires, meet German and Argentine business representatives and visit a Mercedes-Benz plant there.
Kohl then flies on to Brazilia for talks with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and to meet members of Congress and the Senate, and business representatives from September 17 to 18.

The German leader will then fly to Mexico to meet President Ernesto Zedillo on September 19 in Mexico City. He is also set to receive an honorary medal from the city and address the Mexican Senate in a speech.
The following day he is scheduled to meet representatives from Mexican trade and industry and visit the Volkswagen VW plant in Puebla and the federal state of Yucatan.
It will be the chancellor's second visit to Argentina and third to Mexico and Brazil, another government spokesman said in response to an inquiry.
Kohl will be flying back to Germany on September 21.
